Also it's roots go back to the absolute beginnings of guitar music, you can grab it and bang out some Robert Johnson or Elmore James, Son House and Muddy Waters.

I don't own a cigar box guitar. I've looked at a few and considered a few, but I've never found one that I wanted to own. If I do buy one, it'll have six strings - almost certainly.

At one point, I considered making one from a kit, but I decided that I'd never actually get around to making it and that it'd just be a waste of space. So, I didn't go that route.

I suppose the difference is I'm comfortable faithfully replicating music. I don't feel any compelling need to compose. Faithful replication is a challenge and I enjoy that aspect of it. That means I'd probably end up with a cigar box guitar if they were more popular in music.

I don't really seek to be inspired or taken in a new direction. I just learn to master what's on the page.

Sometimes I get creative fits - but those are pretty rare. I seldom "noodle." I usually am playing something as it was written. Even when I'm doing composition, it's usually at the directions of someone else and they're still telling me what they want to hear.

I actually enjoy recomposing things, not always simplification either I like trying to blend aspects of lead and rhythm guitars together, or combing parts of the bass riffs and rythme guitar together, or even sometimes just using a slide to match the vocals of something.

One of the things I'm most grateful for is my good health. I don't like to even imagine life without the ability to play guitar.

A few years back, someone hit me on my motorcycle and I was unable to play for a while. It was one of the most frustrating times of my life. They'd wanted to do surgery on my left hand and the risks were high, so I declined. Fortunately, we were able to work my guitar playing into my PT and I made a full recovery.

If there's a list of things that actually scare me, not being able to play is one of them. Death doesn't scare me, but that does.
